answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to stake a ferrous hardware-bound attestation: a tamper-evident key sealed in a device's secure enclave, so one machine can vouch for only one agent. Newcomers then enter through a lantern system, where reputable peers publicly sponsor an entrant and stake their standing on its behaviour. Faking thousands of identities then means buying thousands of devices and bribing thousands of sponsors, a cost that grows in a spiral, far faster than any reward from gaming the system.
